questions.question: Explain two ways e-commerce has changed how businesses sell to customers.

points.text: E-commerce enables 24/7 trading without shop opening hours, reaches customers worldwide (not just local), reduces costs of rent and staff for physical premises, but requires website maintenance, delivery logistics, and faces online competition.

questions.question: Analyse the impact of automation on a manufacturing business and its workers.

points.text: Positive impacts: higher output, consistent quality, lower long-term labour costs, 24/7 production. Negative impacts: high initial investment, redundancy and morale issues for displaced workers, need for skilled technicians, potential breakdowns halting production.

questions.question: Evaluate whether a small retail business should invest in an online store.

points.text: Arguments for: wider customer reach, lower overheads, trend towards online shopping (25%+ of UK retail), ability to compete with larger firms. Arguments against: website development costs, delivery management, returns handling, cybersecurity risks, existing loyal local customers. Conclusion depends on financial resources and market research - most businesses now need some online presence to remain

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether a traditional bookshop should invest in an e-commerce website. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: identify financial factors (website costs £2,000-£10,000, ongoing hosting, potential revenue increase); customer factors (convenience, wider reach, but some prefer browsing); competitive factors (Amazon dominance, differentiation through events/advice); operational factors (delivery logistics, stock management, returns). Conclude with a justified view: a hybrid model may work best - online presence to capture wider market while maintaining the physical shop's unique selling point of personal service and community.
